## Design

### 2026-10-25 – ### What I worked on:

**1.4h**

### What I worked on:
- Brainstormed ideas for Week 3 (Design Your Instrument) and settled on the "Retro Stylophone" – a compact handheld synth using an ESP32.
- Decided against mechanical tactile switches for the keyboard and chose capacitive PCB touch pads instead (using the ESP32 built-in touch peripheral on GPIOs) to save cost and avoid mechanical soldering clutter.
- Set up the GitHub repository `Retro_Stylophone` and organized the initial project structure.
- Calculated the Bill of Materials (BoM) under the Tier 1 grant limit ($30.00). Sourced full multipacks (2x ESP32 boards, 10x 10k potentiometers, 40x slide switches) via Amazon to avoid import duties and split self-funded parts (custom JLCPCB manufacturing and buzzers) transparently.
- Drew the initial concept sketch (top-down view) on paper:
  - Form factor planned at 120 x 70 mm.
  - Layout arranged with the ESP32 on the left, central piezo buzzer, pitch/modulation pot on the right, and a 13-pad keyboard (8 naturals, 5 accidentals) along the bottom edge.

### 2026-10-25 – ### What I worked on:

**2.4h**

### What I worked on:
- Finished the complete schematic in KiCad for the Retro Stylophone:
  - Wired the 38-pin ESP32 socket headers to all peripheral components.
  - Connected the passive piezo buzzer to DAC1/PWM pin (GPIO 25), the 10k potentiometer to ADC1 (GPIO 34), and the SPDT octave slide switch to GPIO 19.
  - Implemented the 13-note chromatic keyboard: wired the 8 natural notes (C4–C5) and 2 accidentals (C#4, D#4) to native capacitive touch channels (T0–T9), and connected the remaining 3 accidentals (F#4, G#4, A#4) to high-impedance ADC antenna pins (GPIO 36, 39, 35) to get a full 13-key keyboard without external ICs.
- Assigned real physical footprints:
  - 1x19 2.54mm pin headers for the ESP32 socket.
  - Standard 12mm THT buzzer and Alps/Bourns vertical potentiometer footprints.

- Completed the PCB Layout in the board editor:
  - Defined the board outline on `Edge.Cuts` layer (~125 x 75 mm).
  - Routed all signal tracks using 0.3mm traces, switching between front and back layers with vias.
  - Resolved silkscreen clearance warnings and passed the final DRC check with **0 errors and 0 unrouted nets**.

### 2026-10-25 – *(note: Hackatime didn't track properly in the background during this session, so I took screenshots of my files, build setup, and clean compiler output to prove the 6 hours of work).*

**6h**

*(note: Hackatime didn't track properly in the background during this session, so I took screenshots of my files, build setup, and clean compiler output to prove the 6 hours of work).*

### What I did:
- Set up PlatformIO with the `esp32dev` environment and fixed the missing Arduino include paths in VS Code.
- Coded the sound engine (`synth_engine.h` / `synth_engine.cpp`) using ESP32 PWM on GPIO 25. Added portamento gliding, different square-wave duty cycles, noise bursts for percussive sounds, and an arpeggiator function.
- Built the touch keyboard matrix (`touch_keys.h` / `touch_keys.cpp`) for all 13 notes:
  - 10 notes read natively via ESP32 capacitive touch pins (T0–T9).
  - 3 accidentals read through ADC pins (GPIO 35, 36, 39) via body capacitance.
  - Added baseline auto-calibration at boot and continuous baseline drift tracking.
- Tied everything together in `main.cpp` with a 10 ms debounce filter, pitch-bend on the 10k potentiometer, and octave switching on the slide switch.
- Compiled cleanly with 0 errors and 0 warnings.
